title: Benevolent societies and hiring bands
summary: Ernie and Dejan compare benevolent societies with insurance. They say members now sometimes ask for the cash instead of a hired band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Young men and the young men are left. The difference between the society is these are other than just more pleasure clubs.

Well, the society is it. I mean, that's why. The benevolent society. The benevolent society don't have as many members as they used to have because so many people get so much out of insurance. See, the benevolent society, they furnish your barrel and all that, but it's not that much in it. And some of the guys been in there so long and have the money involved and they won't get out, see. So that still makes the organization still going on. They'll still get their benevolent, but they have what the insurance don't give them. They have bunk heads like we have. They have their own bunk heads. They have the anniversaries where they hire a band to go to the church. Then they'll have their parade and their meetings and things like that. Then they'll have a regular to-do. They'll invite their wives and then their friends. In other words, they combine it with pleasure and benevolent and everything combined in one. You see. To give them somewhere to grow something and still be in the society and still get the benefits that they would get in the insurance. You see. Well at one time some guy was belong to the Tree of Forces side. Yeah, he'd have a big field there. The last time I made those recordings over there, I'd see if I have an uncle now on that board up there. Dick Allen showed up there. My great uncle, he's now up over there. Same name as yours. Yeah, Cat and your lady. I'd have to look and wonder who he was.
Yeah, they have a lot of names up there. I see George Dino's father was up there too.
You see, when the fellows belonged to all these different societies, he had an extra lawyer for them because each society was formed as a band, and each society turned out with the band.
Yeah, see that was the thing.
And each band would come at this hall and meet that society, and the other hall and meet that society. These bands come from all directions and come in there.

Well, they still have a few of them like that now. They have some guy that belongs to the masons, and that belongs to the Olympians, and they also belong to the oddfellas, you see. Well if those street societies decide that they want to use bands, that'd be three bands on the street for that particular person.
Yeah, but you know what the people do now? The people said they'd rather have that money.

Well, it's happened. Somebody's hit them about that, see. They tell you, well instead of paying that money out the higher bands, we don't need no money to give us that money. Quite natural, society wouldn't give it to them. Yeah, it's too bad.
Yeah, a long time ago, society nobody asked that question about the money. The society turned out with the band, that was it.
In other words, all they was looking for the barrel and the body. Well, they would give them the barrel and the body, and then they would hire the band and everything else.
Now some of them winners, one society barry, give me the cash money. You don't need no band. That's messing things up, you know.
